purpose: CPU-only diagnostic: does reference-free student disagreement identify teacher benefit, beyond predicting student error or chain length?
scope: All626 reused development targets,606sequence clusters. Existing FP32 predictions and fixed-correspondence metrics only. No new GPU inference, fitting, locked-test scoring or independent-validation claim.
student: Previously frozen reference-free3sample CA-lDDT medoid; retain its existing choices. Disagreement=1-meanoffdiagonal pairwise CA-lDDT. All3student samples are required and must be counted in future end-to-end cost.
teacher: Fixed first teacher sample0, no oracle selection or confidence optimization.
policies: Before opening native scores freeze157/626targets (ceil25%) by highest disagreement, and a same-count longest-chain policy. Tie-break lexicographic ID. Random fallback expectation uses157/626 of average teacher-minus-student benefit. Report full teacher and no-fallback controls.
analysis: TM and CA-lDDT differences with606cluster bootstrap; Pearson disagreement versus student error and teacher improvement, pooled and within<=256/>256 strata; partial Pearson after removing intercept/logL/logL squared. No fitted selector and no choosing a preferred budget after results. Report teacher-call fraction, not a speedup from unmatched timings. Correlation is not calibration.
decision: Useful only if disagreement targets teacher benefit beyond same-budget random/length-only policies. Any positive result still requires independent families and matched end-to-end cost before deployment. A null result closes this simple fallback rule; no threshold or feature grid.
